{{Short description|Kuni no miyatsuko of Owari Province, ancient Japan}}
The '''Owari no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' ({{lang|ja|尾張国造}}, also read ''Owari kokuzō'') were the {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造|lt=kuni no miyatsuko|lt_ja=国造}} who governed {{ill|Owari Province|ja|尾張国|lt=Owari Province|lt_ja=尾張国}}. The name is also written {{lang|ja|尾治国造}}.

== Overview ==
=== Ancestry ===
* The "Kokuzō Hongi" of the ''Sendai Kuji Hongi'' records that in the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|ja|成務天皇|lt=Emperor Seimu|lt_ja=成務天皇}}, '''{{ill|Otoyo no Mikoto|ja|乎止与命|lt=Otoyo no Mikoto|lt_ja=小止与命}}''', thirteenth-generation descendant of {{ill|Amenohoakari|ja|天火明命|lt=Amenohoakari|lt_ja=天火明命}}, was appointed Owari no Kuni no Miyatsuko.

=== Clan ===
The '''{{ill|Owari clan|ja|尾張氏|lt=Owari clan|lt_ja=尾張氏}}''' (おわりうじ), with the {{ill|Kabane|ja|姓|lt=kabane|lt_ja=姓}} {{ill|Muraji|ja|連|lt=muraji|lt_ja=連}}. In Tenmu 13 (684) it received the rank of {{ill|Sukune|ja|宿禰|lt=sukune|lt_ja=宿禰}}. Its relationship with the {{ill|Yamato kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|lt=Yamato kingship|lt_ja=ヤマト政権}} was old: it supplied consorts such as {{ill|Yosotarashi-hime|ja|世襲足媛|lt=Yosotarashi-hime|lt_ja=世襲足媛}}, consort of {{ill|Emperor Kōshō|ja|孝昭天皇|lt=Emperor Kōshō|lt_ja=孝昭天皇}}; {{ill|Owari no Ōama-hime|ja|尾張大海媛|lt=Ōama-hime|lt_ja=大海媛}}, consort of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇|lt=Emperor Sujin|lt_ja=崇神天皇}}; {{ill|Miyazu-hime|ja|美夜受比売|lt=Miyazu-hime|lt_ja=宮簀媛}}, consort of {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|倭建命|lt=Yamato Takeru|lt_ja=日本武尊}}; and {{ill|Owari no Menoko-hime|ja|尾張目子媛|lt=Menoko-hime|lt_ja=目子媛}}, consort of {{ill|Emperor Keitai|ja|継体天皇|lt=Emperor Keitai|lt_ja=継体天皇}}, and was among the most powerful of all the ''kuni no miyatsuko'' houses. The {{ill|Danpusan Kofun|ja|断夫山古墳|lt=Danpusan Kofun|lt_ja=断夫山古墳}} and the {{ill|Shiratori Kofun (Nagoya)|ja|白鳥古墳 (名古屋市)|lt=Shiratori Kofun|lt_ja=白鳥古墳}} are thought to be tombs of the family. It continued to flourish from the {{ill|Nara period|ja|奈良時代|lt=Nara period|lt_ja=奈良時代}} on, and many members became central officials or district officials within Owari.

== Base ==
The seat of the ''kuni no miyatsuko'' was '''{{ill|Aichi District, Aichi|ja|愛知郡 (愛知県)|lt=Ayuchi District|lt_ja=年魚市郡}}''' in Owari Province.

=== Territory ===
The territory of the ''kuni no miyatsuko'' was the region then called '''Owari''', corresponding to present-day {{ill|Nagoya|ja|名古屋市|lt=Nagoya|lt_ja=名古屋市}}, {{ill|Seto, Aichi|ja|瀬戸市|lt=Seto|lt_ja=瀬戸市}}, {{ill|Toyoake|ja|豊明市|lt=Toyoake|lt_ja=豊明市}}, {{ill|Nisshin, Aichi|ja|日進市|lt=Nisshin|lt_ja=日進市}}, {{ill|Tōgō, Aichi|ja|東郷町|lt=Tōgō|lt_ja=東郷町}} and {{ill|Nagakute|ja|長久手市|lt=Nagakute|lt_ja=長久手市}} in Aichi Prefecture: the area excluding the territories of the Niwa and Nakashima ''agata-nushi'' to the north. In the fifth and sixth centuries it governed all of Owari. Ancient Owari as told in the ''{{ill|Kiki|ja|記紀|lt=Kiki|lt_ja=記紀}}'' appears as part of the territory of the {{ill|Yamato kingship|ja|ヤマト王権|lt=Yamato kingship|lt_ja=ヤマト王権}}. {{ill|Atsuta Shrine|ja|熱田神宮|lt=Atsuta Shrine|lt_ja=熱田神宮}}, Owari's representative shrine and the one served by the ''kuni no miyatsuko'', is famous for enshrining the Kusanagi sword ({{ill|Kusanagi no Tsurugi|ja|天叢雲剣|lt=Ama-no-Murakumo no Tsurugi|lt_ja=天叢雲剣}}), one of the {{ill|Imperial Regalia of Japan|ja|三種の神器|lt=Three Sacred Treasures|lt_ja=三種の神器}}. Owari also appears in the {{ill|Legend|ja|伝説|lt=legends|lt_ja=伝説}} of {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|ja|倭姫命|lt=Yamatohime|lt_ja=倭姫命}} and {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|lt=Ise Shrine|lt_ja=伊勢神宮}}, and culturally Owari was strongly influenced by the Kinai, {{ill|Ōmi Province|ja|近江国|lt=Ōmi|lt_ja=近江}} and {{ill|Ise Province|ja|伊勢国|lt=Ise|lt_ja=伊勢}}.

== Clan deity ==
The shrine served by the ''kuni no miyatsuko'' was '''{{ill|Atsuta Shrine|ja|熱田神宮|lt=Atsuta Shrine|lt_ja=熱田神宮}}'''. Its ''ōhafuri'' and chief priest (''daigūji'') families descend from the Owari no Kuni no Miyatsuko, and the descendant {{ill|Senshū clan|ja|千秋氏|lt=Senshū clan|lt_ja=千秋氏}} is connected through the female line.

=== Related shrines ===
* {{ill|Masumida Shrine|ja|真清田神社|lt=Masumida Shrine|lt_ja=真清田神社}}
*: {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|ja|一宮市|lt=Ichinomiya|lt_ja=一宮市}}, Aichi Prefecture. Deity: Amenohoakari. The ''ichinomiya'' of Owari.
* {{ill|Atsuta Shrine|ja|熱田神宮|lt=Atsuta Shrine|lt_ja=熱田神宮}}
*: {{ill|Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|ja|熱田区|lt=Atsuta-ku|lt_ja=熱田区}}, Nagoya. Deity: the Kusanagi sword. The ''sannomiya'' of Owari. Many of its subsidiary shrines are connected with the Owari clan.
* {{ill|Utsutsu Shrine|ja|内々神社|lt=Utsutsu Shrine|lt_ja=内々神社}}
*: {{ill|Kasugai, Aichi|ja|春日井市|lt=Kasugai|lt_ja=春日井市}}, Aichi Prefecture. Deities: Takeinadane, Yamato Takeru, Miyazu-hime.
* {{ill|Haritsuna Shrine|ja|針綱神社|lt=Haritsuna Shrine|lt_ja=針綱神社}}
*: {{ill|Inuyama, Aichi|ja|犬山市|lt=Inuyama|lt_ja=犬山市}}, Aichi Prefecture. Deities: Takeinadane, Otsunane and others.
* {{ill|Owaribe Shrine|ja|尾張戸神社|lt=Owaribe Shrine|lt_ja=尾張戸神社}}
*: {{ill|Seto, Aichi|ja|瀬戸市|lt=Seto|lt_ja=瀬戸市}}, Aichi Prefecture, or {{ill|Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|ja|守山区|lt=Moriyama-ku|lt_ja=守山区}}, Nagoya. Deities: Amenohoakari, Takeinadane, Amenokaguyama.
* {{ill|Hazu Shrine|ja|羽豆神社|lt=Hazu Shrine|lt_ja=羽豆神社}}
*: {{ill|Minamichita, Aichi|ja|南知多町|lt=Minamichita|lt_ja=南知多町}}, Aichi Prefecture. Deity: Takeinadane.
* {{ill|Owari Ōkunitama Shrine|ja|国府宮|lt=Owari Ōkunitama Shrine|lt_ja=尾張大国霊神社}}
*: {{ill|Inazawa|ja|稲沢市|lt=Inazawa|lt_ja=稲沢市}}, Aichi Prefecture. Deity: Owari Ōkunitama.
* {{ill|Owari Shrine|ja|尾張神社|lt=Owari Shrine|lt_ja=尾張神社}}
*: {{ill|Komaki|ja|小牧市|lt=Komaki|lt_ja=小牧市}}, Aichi Prefecture. The deity was perhaps originally the Owari clan's ancestral god.

=== Tombs ===
The oldest kofun in the territory of the Owari no Kuni no Miyatsuko is said to be the Okunoji Kofun (a round mound 25 metres across) in Aisai (formerly Saori, Ama District). Okitsu Shrine stands on its summit, and three {{ill|Sankakubuchi shinjūkyō|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|lt=triangular-rimmed mirrors with deities and beasts|lt_ja=三角縁神獣鏡}} kept by the shrine were found to be cast from the same moulds as {{ill|Bronze mirror|ja|銅鏡|lt=bronze mirrors|lt_ja=銅鏡}} excavated at the {{ill|Tsubai-ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|lt=Tsubai-ōtsukayama Kofun|lt_ja=椿井大塚山古墳}}, so it is estimated to date from the early fourth century. In the north, on the summit of Hakusanbira (142 m) in Inuyama, is the keyhole-shaped (square-back) {{ill|Higashinomiya Kofun|ja|東之宮古墳|lt=Higashinomiya Kofun|lt_ja=東之宮古墳}} (78 m long, a national {{ill|Historic Sites of Japan|ja|史跡|lt=historic site|lt_ja=史跡}}), whose grave goods include eleven bronze mirrors, among them triangular-rimmed mirrors. From the dates and forms of these Owari tombs, the '''{{ill|Shiratorizuka Kofun|ja|白鳥塚古墳|lt=Shiratorizuka Kofun|lt_ja=白鳥塚古墳}}''' is thought to be the tomb of the first ''kuni no miyatsuko'' Otoyo, the '''{{ill|Owaribe Shrine Kofun|ja|尾張戸神社古墳|lt=Owaribe Shrine Kofun|lt_ja=尾張戸神社古墳}}''' that of Otoyo's wife, the '''Higashinomiya Kofun''' that of the next ''kuni no miyatsuko'' {{ill|Takeinadane|ja|建稲種命|lt=Takeinadane|lt_ja=建稲種命}}, and the '''{{ill|Kabutoyama Kofun (Tōkai)|ja|兜山古墳 (東海市)|lt=Kabutoyama Kofun|lt_ja=兜山古墳}}''' that of {{ill|Miyazu-hime|ja|美夜受比売|lt=Miyazu-hime|lt_ja=美夜受比売}}.<ref>{{ill|Takao Hōga|ja|宝賀寿男|lt=Hōga Toshio|lt_ja=宝賀寿男}}, "[http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/hitori/takaosan2.htm Kofun with a shrine on the mound]", ''Koju Kinobōma'', 2015.</ref>

== People ==
* '''{{ill|Otoyo no Mikoto|ja|乎止与命|lt=Otoyo no Mikoto|lt_ja=乎止与命}}'''
*: First Owari no Kuni no Miyatsuko, in the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|ja|成務天皇|lt=Emperor Seimu|lt_ja=成務天皇}}.
* '''{{ill|Takeinadane|ja|建稲種命|lt=Takeinadane no Mikoto|lt_ja=建稲種命}}'''
*: Also Takeinada no Sukune. A courtier under {{ill|Emperor Keikō|ja|景行天皇|lt=Emperor Keikō|lt_ja=景行天皇}} and Emperor Seimu; son of Otoyo and elder brother of Miyazu-hime.
* '''{{ill|Otsunane no Mikoto|ja|尾綱根命|lt=Otsunane no Mikoto|lt_ja=尾綱根命}}''' (Otsuna no Muraji)
*: Minister and ''kuni no miyatsuko'' under {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|lt=Emperor Ōjin|lt_ja=応神天皇}}; son of Takeinadane. Three of his nieces married Emperor Ōjin, and he received the name Owari no Muraji.
* '''{{ill|Otohiko no Muraji|ja|弟彦連|lt=Otohiko no Muraji|lt_ja=弟彦連}}'''
*: ''Kuni no miyatsuko'' under {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|lt=Emperor Nintoku|lt_ja=仁徳天皇}}.

=== Family ===
* {{ill|Miyazu-hime|ja|宮簀媛|lt=Miyazu-hime|lt_ja=宮簀媛}}
*: A woman of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|lt=Kofun period|lt_ja=古墳時代}}, younger sister of Takeinadane. She married {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|lt=Yamato Takeru|lt_ja=日本武尊}} on his return from the eastern campaign, and founded the Atsuta shrine to keep the {{ill|Kusanagi no Tsurugi|ja|草薙剣|lt=Kusanagi sword|lt_ja=草薙剣}}.
* {{ill|Ameoshihito no Mikoto|ja|天忍男命|lt=Ameoshihito no Mikoto|lt_ja=天忍男命}}
*: Son of {{ill|Ōnunushi no Mikoto|ja|大沼主命|lt=Ōnunushi no Mikoto|lt_ja=大沼主命}}; distant ancestor of the {{ill|Tsumori clan|ja|津守氏|lt=Tsumori clan|lt_ja=津守氏}} and others.
* {{ill|Yosotarashi-hime|ja|世襲足媛|lt=Yosotarashi-hime|lt_ja=世襲足媛}}
*: Daughter of Ameoshihito. Empress of Emperor Kōshō and mother of {{ill|Emperor Kōan|ja|孝安天皇|lt=Emperor Kōan|lt_ja=孝安天皇}}.
* {{ill|Taketaori no Mikoto|ja|建多乎利命|lt=Taketaori no Mikoto|lt_ja=建多乎利命}}
*: Son of Taketome; ancestor of the Yumo-Takeda no Muraji, Fue no Muraji, Wakainukai no Muraji and others.

== Descendants ==
* {{ill|Owari no Aso|ja|尾張吾襲|lt=Owari no Aso|lt_ja=尾張吾襲}}
*: An official of the Kofun period, envoy of {{ill|Emperor Ingyō|ja|允恭天皇|lt=Emperor Ingyō|lt_ja=允恭天皇}}; killed by {{ill|Katsuragi no Tamada no Sukune|ja|葛城玉田宿禰|lt=Katsuragi no Tamada no Sukune|lt_ja=葛城玉田宿禰}}.
* {{ill|Owari no Ōsumi|ja|尾張大隅|lt=Owari no Ōsumi|lt_ja=尾張大隅}}
*: A warrior of the Asuka period. In the {{ill|Jinshin War|ja|壬申の乱|lt=Jinshin War|lt_ja=壬申の乱}} he provided a temporary palace and war funds to {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|天武天皇|lt=Prince Ōama|lt_ja=大海人皇子}}. Also ''{{ill|Hafuri|ja|祝 (神職)|lt=ōhafuri|lt_ja=大祝}}'' of the Atsuta shrine.
* {{ill|Owari no Hamanushi|ja|尾張浜主|lt=Owari no Hamanushi|lt_ja=尾張浜主}}
*: A court musician of the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|lt=Heian period|lt_ja=平安時代}}. He led the reform of Heian court music and is said to have lived past 113.
* {{ill|Owari no Kazumoto|ja|尾張員職|lt=Owari no Kazumoto|lt_ja=尾張員職}}
*: A Heian-period priest, the last of the Owari clan to serve as {{ill|Daigūji|ja|大宮司|lt=chief priest|lt_ja=大宮司}} of Atsuta Shrine. Great-great-grandfather of {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|lt_ja=源頼朝}}.
